title: PRD: Metricized prompt sentinels and multi-stage abort policy for Optimize
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define an executable PRD that specifies (1) a metricized prompt sentinel framework for Optimize prompt sets, (2) multi-stage A/B decisioning rules including statistical power and quantile-weighted deltas, and (3) deterministic hard- and soft-abort triggers for progressive rollouts. This PRD unblocks implementation work in the Optimize evaluation pipeline and rollout automation.
background: Current Optimize rollouts rely on a small set of aggregated signals and threshold heuristics. Teams have observed occasional regression surprises in long-tail cohorts and ambiguous A/B failures where rollback decisions are ad-hoc. We need a clear, testable contract for quality signals, cohort construction, sample sizing, and rollback actions to support predictable canaries and automated partial rollbacks.
goals: Define a sentinel prompt taxonomy (smoke, core, long-tail) with minimum sample sizes and acceptance bounds
Specify statistical rules for A/B pass/fail decisions (confidence, effect-size, directionality) appropriate for small-traffic canaries
Design a multi-stage abort policy: soft alerts -> traffic pause -> automatic partial rollback -> full rollback
Produce acceptance criteria and PR-ready evaluation harness requirements for engineering to implement
non_goals: We will not design model training or retraining processes (this PRD focuses on eval and rollout gating)
We will not replace existing customer-facing SLO contracts; this is an internal eval gating layer
requirements: Sentinel prompt sets must be versioned and stored in the Optimize promptset registry
Each rollout must reference an explicit sentinel bundle id with cohort definitions
A/B decision engine must compute both aggregate metrics and stratified cohort deltas with p-values and bootstrap confidence intervals
Rollout automation must support staged percentages (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with configurable monitoring windows per stage
Alerting must emit human-readable rationale for any automated abort action including primary contributing cohort and metric
promptset_spec: Three-tier taxonomy: smoke (10-50 fast-check prompts), core (500 prompts across primary use cases), long-tail (min 2,000 prompts sampled across low-frequency cohorts)
Prompts must include metadata: intent label, expected canonical output (or rubric), difficulty score, example user segments
Prompt provenance recorded: customer-supplied, synthetic, or internal benchmark
Sentinel bundles must include stratification keys: region, language, device class, and user cohort tag
sampling_plan: Randomized sampling for core prompts with stratified quotas to preserve cohort balance
Priority seeding: ensure at least 25% of long-tail samples are edge-case inputs identified from errors in past 90 days
Sample-size guidance: for core cohorts aim for >= 500 examples for 80% power to detect 3% absolute regression; long-tail uses bootstrap estimation and paired comparisons
Opaque-system-handling: ensure sampling excludes PII and respects redaction rules
regression_thresholds: Primary quality metric: composite Q_score (0-100) combining exact-match-weighted semantic score, safety penalty, and calibration term
Hard fail: absolute Q_score drop >= 5 points on core cohort and p-value < 0.01 (two-sided)
Soft warn: Q_score drop between 2 and 5 points OR p-value between 0.01 and 0.05 triggers extended observation window
Long-tail rule: any single long-tail cohort showing >=10% relative increase in unacceptable outputs triggers cohort-level hold regardless of aggregate
ab_criteria: A/B pass requires: (a) no hard fails across core cohorts, (b) aggregate Q_score delta within -2 points with p-value >= 0.05, (c) no safety regressions beyond baseline tolerance
Directional testing: when model changes intentionally increase conservatism, apply one-sided tests with pre-declared direction
Multiplicity correction: use Benjamini-Hochberg for cohort-level tests to control false discovery rate across stratified checks
Minimum traffic rule: do not evaluate A/B until stage has seen at least 1,000 production requests mapped to sentinel prompts
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): smoke run against internal traffic and synthetic prompts; must pass smoke checks
Stage 1 (canary 1%): 48 hour window; compute core+long-tail signals; soft warns require extended monitoring; hard fail triggers immediate rollback
Stage 2 (5%): 72 hour window; require no hard fails and cumulative Q_score delta < -2; if soft warns persist, pause at 5% and run targeted remediation
Stage 3 (20%): 7 day window; run full stratified analysis; automated partial rollback to previous variant allowed if cohort-level regressions are observed
Stage 4 (100%): final promotion only after 7-day stability and no unresolved cohort fails
rollback_triggers: Immediate full rollback: any hard fail on core cohort detected during a stage
Partial rollback (traffic reweight): if a single cohort exceeds long-tail threshold while aggregate remains nominal, reduce traffic for affected cohort routing and notify SE/PM
Automated pause: two consecutive soft warns across different metrics within the same stage leads to staged pause and manual review
Emergency rollback: low-latency safety incidents (user-reported high-severity content) documented in incident channel trigger immediate full rollback and postmortem
metrics_to_monitor: Cohort-specific unacceptable-output counts and percent change
User-facing regressions (customer tickets) mapped to sentinel prompts
observability: Per-rollout dashboard template with stage timeline, metric sparkline, cohort heatmap, and annotated abort actions
Automated email + #optimize-rollouts Slack alert on soft warn and hard fail with links to implicated prompts and PR artifacts
Retention: store stage-level eval artifacts and raw prompt/responses for 90 days for audit and debugging
Tracing hooks to correlate production request IDs with sentinel evaluations when available
acceptance_criteria: Engineers can supply a sentinel bundle id to the rollout API and receive stage-level gating decisions
Automated tests covering statistical decisioning exist with simulated traffic for each stage
Dashboards render cohort heatmaps and show clear reason strings for any abort action
On-call runbook automations implement partial rollback and traffic reweight steps described in this PRD
End-to-end smoke test demonstrating a controlled partial rollback in a non-production sandbox
test_plan: Unit tests for A/B decision logic including p-value and bootstrap CI implementations
Integration test that runs a staged rollout against synthetic and historical traffic (replay) and asserts expected abort/no-abort outcomes
Chaos test: inject edge-case prompts from long-tail set to verify cohort-level holds and partial rollback behavior
Manual UAT with PM and design reviewing dashboard and abort rationale language
notes: Open question: whether to include weighted user-value multiplier in Q_score for commercial cohorts — proposed follow-up with monetization team. Also propose a follow-up spike (1 sprint) to benchmark sample-size guidance for long-tail using historical variance estimates.
